articles.title: The JWST May Have Found Where Heavy Black Hole Seeds Formed
articles.description: Astrophysicists think that black holes grow through a hierarchical merger framework. But the elusive Intermediate Mass Black Holes are the missing link between stellar mass black holes, and the gargantuan supermassive black holes like the one at the center of the Milky Way. The JWST may have found the ancient sources of IMBH heavy seeds: young massive clusters in the high-redshift Universe.
articles.summary: JWST observations may have discovered where intermediate-mass black hole seeds formed, solving a major mystery in black hole formation and hierarchical growth.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover breaks historic record after traveling 28 miles
articles.description: NASA’s Perseverance rover has set a historic record by traveling 28.10 miles across Mars, farther than any vehicle has ever driven on another world. Armed with groundbreaking autonomous navigation technology and increasingly advanced driving capabilities, the rover is pushing the boundaries of robotic exploration.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover sets a historic record by traveling 28.10 miles across Mars, surpassing all previous planetary vehicle distance achievements.

articles.title: Scientists say a forgotten particle may explain why the universe exists
articles.description: A mysterious particle overlooked for decades may hold the key to why matter survived the Big Bang, allowing stars, planets, and life to exist. Scientists believe this forgotten neutrino reshaped the early universe and may have left detectable gravitational wave signals that could help unlock the cosmos’s deepest mysteries.
articles.summary: A long-overlooked particle may explain why matter survived the Big Bang, providing a crucial key to understanding why our universe contains stars, planets, and life.

articles.title: NASA’s Hubble Uncovers Case of Missing Oxygen in Nearby Dwarf Galaxies
articles.description: NASA’s Hubble studied 37 nearby dwarf galaxies and found that much of the oxygen they expected to see is missing.
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble discovers unexpected oxygen depletion in 37 nearby dwarf galaxies, revealing new insights into galactic chemical evolution. This discovery challenges existing models of galaxy development.

articles.title: Ghostly Cat’s Head Nebula lurks within sight of Hubble and Webb
articles.description: The NASA/ESA Hubble and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescopes recently stared at an eerie star-forming scene within the Carina Nebula, a massive gas and dust cloud located approximately 7500 light-years away from Earth. The two telescopes offer complementary views of the shadowy form, nicknamed the Cat’s Head Nebula, which reflects the 'magical'' process of star formation. Hubble’s visible-light view shows the cat as a dark, elongated dust pillar and hints of young forming stars, while Webb’s infrared-light imagery unveils many stars and other hidden details.
articles.summary: Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes jointly observe the Cat's Head Nebula, a spectacular star-forming region. The combined observations reveal unprecedented detail of stellar nurseries.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The MMX mission successfully launches toward Mars's moon Phobos for exploration. This groundbreaking mission will investigate Phobos's composition and prepare for future sample return.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope discovers its first previously unknown comet. This discovery demonstrates Euclid's powerful capability to reveal hidden cosmic objects.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Solar Orbiter spacecraft has made groundbreaking observations of mysterious S-shaped magnetic structures called switchbacks in the solar atmosphere, advancing our understanding of solar physics.

articles.title: Researchers May Have Solved a Puzzling Contradiction in the Ryugu Sample
articles.description: Samples from the asteroid Ryugu, and from carbonaceous chondrites that have crashed on Earth, present an apparent contradiction. Their fine-grained matrices have widely varied compositions of their clay-like minerals. That suggests that there were widely different aqueous environments in the same parent bodies, which seems unlikely. But new research may have solved that contradiction.
articles.summary: New research resolves a scientific contradiction between asteroid Ryugu samples and carbonaceous meteorites, revealing insights into early solar system chemistry.

articles.title: Space Outposts Beyond the Moon May Rely on Planetary AI
articles.description: NASA plans to return astronauts to the lunar surface in 2028 for the first time since Apollo 17 in 1972. But the famed agency has no intention of stopping there, as they plan to establish a permanent human presence on the Moon through a slow and meticulous process involving power, resource extraction, and habitat technologies. However, with the soaring use of artificial intelligence (AI) in our everyday lives, how could this emerging technology be used to identify new landing sites for future outposts on the Moon and possibly Mars?
articles.summary: NASA is planning to establish lunar surface outposts by 2028, with artificial intelligence playing a crucial role in managing remote space infrastructure beyond the Moon.

articles.title: Hera Probe Sees Asteroid Pair Separately for First Time
articles.description: Planetary defense is a growing concern among the scientific community, as efforts have been made to design and implement missions meant to deflect incoming threats to the Earth well in advance. In 2022, NASA intentionally collided the Double Asteroid Redirection test (DART) planetary defense spacecraft into the smaller asteroid of the binary asteroid, Didymos and Dimorphos, with the latter being the smaller one. While the goal was to ascertain if deflecting an asteroid is feasible, how did this influence the geological characteristics of Dimorphos, and what can it teach us about planetary defense missions?
articles.summary: The Hera probe has achieved the first separate observations of a binary asteroid system, advancing planetary defense capabilities and our ability to study asteroids in detail.

articles.title: What Could Split a Black Hole in Two?
articles.description: We all know that black holes can collide. It has happened since black holes began to form, early in cosmic time. The result is always a clash that gives off gravitational waves and a giant bang. Since black holes have such strong gravity, it's almost impossible to imagine a way that any force could break one apart. Yet, that's the task that a group of scientists in Europe set for themselves.
articles.summary: Theoretical research explores the rare and fascinating phenomenon of black hole collisions and mergers occurring since the earliest moments of cosmic history.

articles.title: Scientists build whole-Earth simulation to help find life on other planets
articles.description: It's a dizzyingly busy time for scientists searching for life on distant planets. To date, astronomers have cataloged more than 6,000 planets beyond our solar system and are searching the atmospheres of the most promising worlds for chemicals that might be byproducts of life. Astrobiologists are particularly interested in atmospheres like Earth's that trap enough heat to support liquid water on the planet's surface, which scientists consider the key factor in determining whether a planet can support life as we know it.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Scientists have built a comprehensive whole-Earth simulation model to improve the search for biosignatures and life on distant exoplanets, accelerating astrobiology research.

articles.title: Dust-shrouded Milky Way star cluster may be nearly as old as the universe
articles.description: Astronomers have determined that VVV CL001, a metal-poor globular cluster near the center of the Milky Way, is about 13.4 billion years old, making it one of the oldest known star clusters in our galaxy. The cluster lies behind thick clouds of interstellar dust, which made its distance and age difficult to establish. The paper, outlining the methodology for estimating its age and distance, was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 20. It has been accepted for publication by Astronomy & Astrophysics.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered that the dust-shrouded globular cluster VVV CL001 near the Milky Way's center is approximately 13 billion years old, making it nearly as ancient as the universe itself.

articles.title: Heavy hydrogen in 3I/ATLAS's methane points to a frigid birthplace
articles.description: The interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS carries a chemical clue to conditions in the planetary system of its origin, locked away long before it reached our sun. Its methane signature is unusually rich in heavy hydrogen, suggesting that the comet's frozen ingredients took shape in an intensely cold environment around another star—or in the cloud that preceded it.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Heavy hydrogen isotopes in interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS reveal clues about the frigid planetary system where it originated, expanding our understanding of comet chemistry and solar system formation.

articles.title: IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos
articles.description: Mysterious particles called neutrinos constantly stream through our bodies, and scientists are now detecting incredibly powerful versions arriving from distant cosmic sources using a massive observatory buried in Antarctic ice. These elusive “ghost particles” could hold extraordinary clues about the Big Bang, extreme cosmic events, and some of the universe’s greatest mysteries.
articles.summary: IceCube detector has captured ghost particles (neutrinos) with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos, opening new windows into understanding extreme cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: NASA's Hubble and Webb discover ancient worlds that remember their past
articles.description: NASA’s Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes have uncovered surprising clues about the solar system’s origins by studying 27 tiny, distant objects beyond Neptune. Scientists discovered that these ancient building blocks of planets have remained remarkably unchanged for billions of years, while their unexpected sizes and numbers challenge existing theories of planet formation.
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes have discovered ancient galaxies that retain clues about the solar system's origins, revealing new insights into early universe formation.

articles.title: Scientists smash oxygen nuclei to recreate matter from the Big Bang
articles.description: Scientists have recreated a primordial state of matter from the dawn of the universe by colliding oxygen nuclei at nearly the speed of light. The surprising results show that this exotic substance can form in smaller, lower-energy collisions than previously demonstrated, challenging the known boundaries of early-universe physics.
articles.summary: Scientists have recreated primordial matter from the dawn of the universe by colliding oxygen nuclei at nearly light speed, unlocking secrets of the Big Bang era.

articles.title: Hubble reveals a stunning twist in how the universe emerged from darkness
articles.description: A surprising discovery by astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope is challenging a leading explanation for how the early universe emerged from a dense fog of hydrogen roughly 13 billion years ago. Scientists once believed powerful winds from exploding stars helped radiation escape galaxies and clear that cosmic fog, but new observations reveal that these winds actually block radiation instead.
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope has uncovered a surprising discovery about the universe's emergence from darkness, challenging leading theories about cosmic evolution.

articles.title: Physicists created a tiny universe and watched time emerge without a clock
articles.description: Scientists have created a miniature universe in the laboratory that could help answer one of the biggest mysteries in physics: What is time, and where does it come from? Using 24,000 ultracold atoms, a University of Birmingham researcher built an isolated quantum system that repeatedly expands and contracts, mimicking the Big Bang and a possible Big Crunch. Remarkably, the experiment showed that time could emerge from changes happening inside the system, without relying on an external clock.
articles.summary: Physicists have created a miniature universe in the laboratory where time emerges naturally without an external clock, potentially solving a fundamental mystery of physics.

articles.title: James Webb Space Telescope uncovers new clues about the origins of 'interstellar invader' comet 3I/ATLAS
articles.description: The findings are another clue towards understanding the origins of 3I/ATLAS and the planet-forming conditions around other stars.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has uncovered new clues about the origins of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS and the planet-forming conditions around distant stars.

articles.title: Researchers May Have Discovered the 6th Dwarf Planet
articles.description: The other five are Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake.
articles.summary: Researchers have identified a potential sixth dwarf planet in our solar system, expanding our understanding of distant icy bodies beyond the traditionally recognized five dwarf planets.

articles.title: Two Different Kinds of Gamma-Ray Bursts Erupted 4 Minutes Apart. Astronomers Have Never Seen This Before.
articles.description: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most energetic cosmic events since the Big Bang, releasing the most energetic type of radiation, gamma rays – the stuff that turned unassuming Bruce Banner into the rampaging Hulk, but on an astronomical, potentially plan…
articles.summary: Astronomers observed two different types of gamma-ray bursts erupting just 4 minutes apart—an unprecedented cosmic event that provides new insights into some of the universe's most energetic phenomena.

articles.title: Possible dwarf planet discovered beyond Pluto
articles.description: Astronomers have found a large icy object beyond Pluto, dubbed 2026 ED138, that could become the solar system’s sixth dwarf planet Read Full Article at RT.com
articles.summary: Astronomers discovered a large icy object named 2026 ED138 beyond Pluto that could qualify as our solar system's sixth dwarf planet, adding to our knowledge of distant Kuiper Belt bodies.

articles.title: Rubin Observatory Spots Possible Dwarf Planet Beyond Pluto—the Biggest in 20 Years
articles.description: The distant, icy celestial body could be our solar system's sixth dwarf planet.
articles.summary: The Rubin Observatory identified a potential dwarf planet candidate beyond Pluto that represents the largest such discovery in 20 years, expanding our solar system's known inventory.

articles.title: Giant new dwarf planet discovered in our own solar system — hiding in plain sight
articles.description: A large object in the Kuiper Belt — a distant region of icy and rocky bodies past Neptune — appears to be a new candidate dwarf planet.
articles.summary: A giant dwarf planet candidate has been discovered hiding in the Kuiper Belt, a distant region of icy bodies past Neptune, revealing previously unknown objects in our solar system.

articles.title: The Rubin Observatory Finds Its First Dwarf Planet Candidate
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory found a distant Solar System object before its decade-long Legacy Survey of Space and Time even got started. The object is a dwarf planet candidate named 2026 ED138, and if confirmed, it will be one of the largest dwarf planets beyo…
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory discovered its first dwarf planet candidate during early observations, ahead of its decade-long comprehensive survey of the cosmos.

articles.title: Astronomers Discover a Giant New Dwarf Planet Candidate Hiding Beyond Pluto
articles.description: What else could be out there?ScienceAlert stories are written, fact-checked, and edited by humans, never generated by AI. Don't miss a story, subscribe here.
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified a giant new dwarf planet candidate beyond Pluto, highlighting the ongoing discoveries awaiting us in the outer reaches of our solar system.

articles.title: NASA crew emerges after 378 days in simulated Mars mission
articles.description: Four crew members emerge after 378 days in NASA's simulated Mars mission, offering insights into astronaut health, isolation and future deep-space exploration.
articles.summary: Four crew members completed NASA's 378-day simulated Mars mission, providing valuable data on astronaut health, psychological resilience, and isolation effects for future human exploration of Mars.

articles.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Crew “Returns” to Earth
articles.description: The four-member Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) crew poses outside for the first time in more than a year following the end of their simulated Mars journey on Oct. 31, 2026. Crew members Matthew Montgomery (left), James Spicer (middle left), Ross Elder (middle right), and Ellen Ellis (right) spent more than a year […]
articles.summary: NASA's CHAPEA crew completes their analog mission and returns to Earth after extended isolation. The crew demonstrates valuable insights for long-duration space exploration.
